record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Complexity of minimum spanning ratio tree
record.original_question: Given a finite planar point set, determine whether computing a plane spanning tree whose spanning ratio is minimum among all plane spanning trees on that point set is NP-hard.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. Is computing the plane spanning tree of minimum spanning ratio for a given point set an NP-hard problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in general position, a plane spanning tree of $P$ is a straight-line tree $T$ with vertex set $P$ whose edges (drawn as line segments) are pairwise non-crossing and which connects all points of $P$. For a connected straight-line graph $G$ on $P$, the spanning ratio (also called dilation or stretch factor) of $G$ is
$$\operatorname{sr}(G)\;=\;\max_{u
eq v\in P} rac{d_G(u,v)}{\|u-v\|_2},$$
where $d_G(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $u$ and $v$ (with edge weights equal to Euclidean lengths) and $\|u-v\|_2$ is the Euclidean distance.

Consider the following decision problem: given a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{Q}^2$ and a rational number $\delta\geq 1$, decide whether there exists a plane spanning tree $T$ of $P$ with $\operatorname{sr}(T)\leq\delta$. Equivalently, the optimization problem asks to compute a plane spanning tree of $P$ minimizing $\operatorname{sr}(T)$ among all plane spanning trees on $P$.

Prove or disprove that this problem is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: The unrestricted (possibly crossing) minimum-dilation spanning tree problem is known to be NP-hard (Cheong, Haverkort, Lee, 2007/2008), and computing minimum-dilation graphs with a bounded number of edges is NP-hard whether or not crossings are allowed. However, the NP-hardness reductions in these works do not enforce planarity of the optimal tree, so the complexity of computing a minimum-spanning-ratio plane spanning tree of a planar point set appears to remain open. No proof of NP-hardness or polynomial-time algorithm specifically for the plane (non-crossing) version has been located.

status_evidence.title: Computing a Minimum-Dilation Spanning Tree is NP-hard
status_evidence.snippet: It is NP-hard to determine whether a spanning tree of a set S of n points in the plane has dilation at most delta. The result does not imply NP-hardness for the plane (non-crossing) version since the optimal tree need not be plane.
status_evidence.claim: The unrestricted minimum-dilation spanning tree problem is NP-hard, but the plane variant is not directly settled by this reduction.

status_evidence.title: Computing Geometric Minimum-Dilation Graphs Is NP-Hard
status_evidence.snippet: Computing a minimum-dilation graph connecting an n-point set in the plane using at most m edges is NP-hard, with or without edge crossings allowed.
status_evidence.claim: Related minimum-dilation graph problems are NP-hard in both plane and non-plane settings, but the spanning tree case with planarity is treated separately.

status_evidence.title: Computing Minimum Dilation Spanning Trees in Geometric Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: No exact polynomial algorithm is known; instances up to about 20 points are solved via integer programming.
status_evidence.claim: As of these works, no efficient algorithm or hardness proof for the plane minimum-dilation spanning tree is reported.
